source_text: Nec ab ira solummodo, sed omni omnino confusione animi libera esse debet orationis intentio de tali spiritu emissa, qualis est spiritus ad quem mittitur. neque enim agnosci poterit spiritu sancto spiritus inquinatus aut tristis a laeto aut impeditus a libero. nemo aduersarium recipit, nemo nisi comparem suum admittit.
thought_title: Prayer requires a spirit matching the Holy Spirit
orientation: Tertullian is continuing his argument that prayer must be offered from a pure and peaceful heart, now extending the requirement from freedom from anger to freedom from every disturbance of the mind.
pass_a_gloss: Not only from anger, but from every disturbance of the mind altogether, the intention of prayer ought to be free, sent out from such a spirit as is the Spirit to whom it is sent. For neither will a polluted spirit be able to be recognized by the Holy Spirit, nor a sad one by a joyful one, nor a hindered one by a free one. No one receives an adversary; no one admits anyone except his equal.

choices.why: Confusio here means mental turmoil or agitation, not just confusion in the modern sense; 'disturbance' captures the agitation that disrupts prayer.
Intentio is the directed attention or purpose of prayer; 'intention' preserves the Latin term's focus on the mind's aim.

choices.term: de tali spiritu emissa, qualis est spiritus ad quem mittitur
choices.english: sent out from such a spirit as is the Spirit to whom it is sent
choices.why: The comparison is between the quality of the praying spirit and the Holy Spirit who receives it; 'such...as' preserves the correlative force of talis...qualis.
rejected: sent from a spirit like the one it is sent to
sent out from a spirit matching the one to whom it is sent

choices.term: agnosci poterit spiritu sancto spiritus inquinatus
choices.english: a polluted spirit will be able to be recognized by the Holy Spirit
choices.why: Agnosci means to be acknowledged or recognized as one's own; the passive with ablative agent preserves the idea that the Holy Spirit does the recognizing.
rejected: the Holy Spirit will be able to recognize a polluted spirit
a polluted spirit can be known by the Holy Spirit

choices.term: nemo aduersarium recipit, nemo nisi comparem suum admittit
choices.english: No one receives an adversary; no one admits anyone except his equal
choices.why: Recipit and admittit are near-synonyms for welcoming or letting in; 'receives' and 'admits' distinguish them while keeping the parallel structure.
rejected: No one welcomes an enemy; no one lets in anyone but his peer
No one accepts an opponent; no one admits except his match

pass_b_english: The intention of prayer must be free not only from anger but from every disturbance of the mind whatsoever. It must be sent out from a spirit of the same kind as the Spirit to whom it is sent. A polluted spirit cannot be recognized by the Holy Spirit, nor a sad one by the joyful, nor a hindered one by the free. No one receives an adversary; no one admits anyone except his equal.
